input_signals.name: Clean Working-Capital Margin
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at)))), RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5), VOL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Stable, persistent gross margins are most credible when they require little noncash working-capital accumulation.
input_signals.reasoning: The accrual channel penalizes large changes in noncash current assets net of nondebt current liabilities. Its interaction with volatility-adjusted gross margin distinguishes durable operating economics from margins supported by receivable, inventory, or other working-capital accounting effects.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( abs( ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), at ) ) ) ), rank( sub( ma( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ), vol( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Demand-Accrual Volatility Alignment
input_signals.expression: RANK(NEG(MAX(RANK(VOL(RATIO(revt, at), 3)), RANK(SUB(VOL(RATIO(ADD(ABS(recch), ABS(invch)), at), 3), VOL(RATIO(revt, at), 3))))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Stable revenue is most credible when receivable and inventory accrual activity is also stable and does not fluctuate more than the underlying demand process.
input_signals.reasoning: The first channel penalizes unstable revenue productivity, while the second isolates excess volatility in receivable and inventory adjustments relative to revenue volatility. The maximum makes either unstable demand or disproportionate operating-accrual noise sufficient to weaken the signal, distinguishing durable operations from working-capital timing effects.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: rank( neg( max( rank( vol( ratio( revt, at ), 3 ) ), rank( sub( vol( ratio( add( abs( recch ), abs( invch ) ), at ), 3 ), vol( ratio( revt, at ), 3 ) ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Converted Margin Improvement
input_signals.hypothesis: Improving gross margins should predict higher returns when they are accompanied by low working-capital investment relative to sales.
input_signals.reasoning: Cross-sectional ranks place margin improvement and working-capital accruals on a common scale, eliminating domination by the unbounded working-capital ratio. Using the working-capital change rather than its sign-unstable level focuses the second channel on incremental cash absorption, while the minimum requires both margin improvement and clean cash conversion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( trend( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ) ), rank( neg( ma( ratio( delta( wcap, 1 ), sale ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Margin Improvement Funding Test
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), sale))), INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms with improving gross margins, those requiring less noncash working-capital investment should earn higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The signed accrual measure rewards working-capital releases and penalizes investment rather than treating both as costs. Industry standardization centers the accrual score, so firms without margin improvement receive a neutral zero while improving-margin firms are ordered by whether their gains convert into cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( neg( ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), sale ) ) ), indicator( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 1 ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Expansion-Gated Depreciation Congruence
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms with improving sales productivity, depreciation growth that remains aligned with sales growth should predict higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The earlier unconditional congruence score could favor firms where depreciation and sales were merely contracting together, contaminating its long portfolio despite a positive cross-sectional slope. The expansion gate removes matched contractions, while the centered alignment score orders only firms for which depreciation consistency has a positive operating-growth interpretation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( neg( winsor( ma( abs( sub( growth( dpc, 1 ), growth( sale, 1 ) ) ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ), indicator( trend( ratio( sale, at ), 3 ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Depreciation-Supported Margin Improvement
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross-margin improvement should predict higher returns when it is not accompanied by a declining depreciation charge relative to sales.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the expansion gate with a ranked margin-change channel removes the growth exposure that may have produced a strong Fama-MacBeth slope but weak FF5 alpha. The second channel tests conservative expense recognition: apparent margin gains are less credible when depreciation intensity is simultaneously being reduced.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 1 ) ), rank( trend( ratio( dpc, sale ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Verified Working-Capital Harvest
input_signals.expression: MUL(ZSCORE(MIN(RANK(LAG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), sale), 1)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), sale))))), INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms with improving gross margins, prior working-capital investment should be favorable only when it reverses into a current working-capital release.
input_signals.reasoning: The minimum explicitly requires both a prior-period buildup and a current-period release, rather than rewarding the lagged accrual magnitude additively. Centering the verified reversal score before applying the margin gate keeps other firms neutral and distinguishes temporary investment realization from persistent high accruals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( zscore( min( rank( lag( ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), sale ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), sale ) ) ) ) ), indicator( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 1 ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Efficient Depreciation Congruence
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(MIN(RANK(NEG(WINSOR(MA(ABS(SUB(GROWTH(dpc, 1), GROWTH(sale, 1))), 3), 1))), RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at)))))), INDICATOR(TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 3), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among expanding firms, depreciation growth congruence should predict higher returns when expansion also requires little noncash working-capital accrual.
input_signals.reasoning: Depreciation congruence alone generated strong Fama-MacBeth evidence but weak long-short alpha, consistent with its extremes retaining generic expansion exposure. The added working-capital bottleneck requires expansion to be both accounting-consistent and cash-efficient, which should improve abnormal-return separation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( min( rank( neg( winsor( ma( abs( sub( growth( dpc, 1 ), growth( sale, 1 ) ) ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ), rank( neg( abs( ratio( sub( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), at ) ) ) ) ) ), indicator( trend( ratio( sale, at ), 3 ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Asset-Release Margin Funding Quality
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(NEG(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1))), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), sale)), INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms with improving gross margins, cash conversion driven by noncash current-asset release rather than nondebt current-liability growth should predict higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: A low net working-capital accrual can arise either from collecting or liquidating noncash current assets, or from stretching suppliers and other current creditors. The expression separates those sources, rewarding asset-side realization and liability paydown while penalizing creditor-funded margin improvement.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( neg( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), sale ) ), indicator( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 1 ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Margin-Decline Working-Capital Squeeze
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(NEG(MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), sale)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1)), sale))))), INDICATOR(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1)), 0))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms with declining gross margins, simultaneous noncash current-asset accumulation and nondebt current-liability growth should predict lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The high-high conjunction identifies firms whose deteriorating operations both trap resources in noncash current assets and increasingly rely on current creditors for financing. This source-specific squeeze mechanism differs from sorting on the level or volatility of aggregate working-capital accruals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( neg( min( rank( ratio( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ), sale ) ), rank( ratio( sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), sale ) ) ) ) ), indicator( neg( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 1 ) ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Accrual-Light Margin Inflection
input_signals.hypothesis: Positive margin inflections should predict higher returns when they occur without a sharp acceleration or liquidation in working-capital intensity.
input_signals.reasoning: Margin acceleration identifies an early operating recovery rather than another current-level margin-improvement screen. Low absolute working-capital acceleration distinguishes a genuine operating inflection from one created by aggressive balance-sheet investment or distress-driven liquidation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( neg( abs( accel( ratio( wcap, sale ) ) ) ) ), indicator( accel( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ) ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Growth-Confirmed Asset-Release Funding
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(NEG(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1))), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), sale)), MUL(INDICATOR(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1), 0), INDICATOR(GROWTH(sale, 1), 0)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms with both margin improvement and sales growth, current-asset realization with limited reliance on current-liability growth should predict higher subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The prior negative long-short alpha may reflect extreme asset releases by shrinking firms whose margins improved through retrenchment rather than durable operations. Requiring actual sales growth removes that liquidation channel and tests asset-side cash realization only when the underlying business is expanding.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( ratio( sub( neg( sub( delta( act, 1 ), delta( che, 1 ) ) ), sub( delta( lct, 1 ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ) ), sale ) ), mul( indicator( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 1 ), 0 ), indicator( growth( sale, 1 ), 0 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Smooth-Earnings Noncash-Asset Share Drift
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms with smooth earnings, growth in the noncash share of current assets should predict lower subsequent returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This stock-composition formulation measures whether current assets are shifting away from cash toward receivables, inventory, and other accrual assets, rather than relying on the conjunction of two flow changes. It provides a broader-coverage test of the same economic mechanism while producing a continuous ordering that may strengthen cross-sectional evidence.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_zscore( neg( growth( ratio( sub( act, che ), act ), 1 ) ) ), indicator( neg( zscore( vol( ratio( ni, at ), 3 ) ) ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Durable-Margin Cash-Share Floor
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5), VOL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))), TS_RANK(RATIO(che, act), 5))
input_signals.hypothesis: Durable gross margins should predict higher returns when the firm’s cash share of current assets is also high relative to its own history.
input_signals.reasoning: The cash-share state is continuous, so the construction does not discard information through a hard margin-quality gate. The bottleneck requires both persistent operating economics and historically strong liquidity composition, replacing the prior flow-substitution screen with a stock-based corroboration mechanism.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( sub( ma( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ), vol( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ) ) ), ts_rank( ratio( che, act ), 5 ) )

input_signals.name: Margin-Gain Liquid-Asset Confirmation
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should earn higher subsequent returns when gross-margin improvement is accompanied by an increasing cash share of current assets.
input_signals.reasoning: Both channels are continuous, similarly scaled changes, avoiding another binary gate applied to the archived substitution score. A rising cash share provides balance-sheet confirmation that the margin gain is improving liquidity composition rather than being absorbed by receivables, inventory, or other current accrual assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 1 ) ), rank( delta( ratio( che, act ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Persistent Profit Liquidity Floor
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms should earn higher subsequent returns when both profitability and the cash share of current assets remain strong even in their weakest recent periods.
input_signals.reasoning: The dual downside floor focuses on durable cash-backed quality rather than blending two signals that share the same current-asset-change term. It requires persistent reported earnings and persistent liquidity simultaneously, reducing sensitivity to one-period accrual movements or temporary cash spikes.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ts_min( ratio( ni, at ), 3 ) ), rank( ts_min( ratio( che, act ), 3 ) ) )
